accepted.question_text: Let phi(k, G) denote the number of k-matchings in a graph G. For integers q >= 1, r >= 1, and 1 <= k <= qr, is the maximum number of k-matchings among all simple r-regular graphs on 2qr vertices attained by the disjoint union of q copies of the complete bipartite graph K_{r,r}? Equivalently, does Theta(k, qr, r) = phi(k, qK_{r,r}) hold for every k = 1, ..., qr, where Theta(k, n, r) is the maximum of phi(k, G) over simple r-regular graphs G on 2n vertices?

evidence.quote: The upper matching conjecture, abbreviated as UMC, states [23] Theta(k, qr, r) = phi(k, qKr,r ) for k = 1, . . . , qr.

Denote by G(2n, r) ... the set of simple r-regular graphs on 2n vertices ... The purpose of this survey paper is to report mostly on the following maximal and minimal problems Theta(k, n, r) := max{phi(k, G), G in G(2n, r)}.

accepted.question_text: Let G be an infinite r-regular graph, and let h_G(p) denote its p-matching entropy, defined from finite graph approximations G_k by h_G(p) = limsup_{k->infty} log(phi(m_k, G_k)) / |V_k| when 2m_k / |V_k| -> p. If h_{inf K_{r,r}}(p) is the corresponding entropy for a countable disjoint union of copies of K_{r,r}, is it always true that h_G(p) <= h_{inf K_{r,r}}(p) for every p in [0, 1]?

accepted.question_text: Let omega(k, n, r) be the minimum number of k-matchings among r-regular r-colorable multigraphs on 2n vertices. For fixed r >= 2, fixed density p in (0, 2/3), and integers k in the range pn <= k <= 2n/3, does omega(k, n, r) grow exponentially in n, and can one prove a quantitatively good lower bound for that exponential growth?

evidence.quote: It is natural to conjecture that for any p in (0, 2/3) and an integer k in [pn, 2n/3] omega(k, n, r) has an exponential growth in n for a fixed r >= 2.
The real challenge is to give a good lower bound for the exponential growth.

accepted.question_text: Let Psi_{2n} be the convex set of 2n x 2n symmetric doubly stochastic matrices with zero diagonal whose extreme points are the adjacency matrices of perfect matchings in K_{2n}. For each 2 <= k <= n, determine or give a good general lower bound for mu_{k,n} := min_{B in Psi_{2n}} haf_k(B), where haf_k(B) is the k-haffnian of B.

evidence.quote: Let Psi2n subset Omega2n,s,0 be the convex set of symmetric doubly stochastic matrices with zero diagonal, whose extreme points are the adjacency matrices of perfect matches in K2n.
Our problem is to find or give a good lower bound for min_{B in Psi2n} haf_k(B) = mu_{k,n} for k = 2, . . . , n.

accepted.question_text: Let mu_{n,n} be the minimum of the haffnian over Psi_{2n}, and let mu := lim_{n->infty} log(mu_{n,n}) / n, whose existence follows from subadditivity. Is mu finite from below; equivalently, does one have mu > -infinity?
accepted.context_brief: Weak van der Waerden analog for haffnians

evidence.quote: Since mu_{n,n} is the minimum of the haffnian function, it follows that mu_{n+m,n+m} <= mu_{n,n} mu_{m,m}. Hence the sequence log mu_{n,n} is subadditive. In particular the following limit exists mu := lim_{n->infty} log mu_{n,n} / n.
A weak analog of the van der Waerden conjecture is the claim that mu > -infinity.

accepted.question_text: Find an analog of the asymptotic lower matching conjecture for arbitrary infinite r-regular graphs, at least for matching densities p in [0, 2/3]. In other words, determine a lower-bound principle for p-matching entropy in the non-bipartite infinite regular setting that plays the role that ALMC plays for bipartite infinite regular graphs.

evidence.quote: There should be a similar inequality for infinite r-regular graphs, at least for p in [0, 2/3] as we explain in Section 7. However we do not have the precise version of such inequality.
We close this section with open problems for infinite regular non-bipartite graphs. First one, find an analog of the LAMC for any infinite r-regular infinite graph for p in [0, 2/3].
